opportunity.title: Founding CTO / AI Engineer
opportunity.employment_type: Full-time employee; JOIN lists London hybrid

evaluation.summary: IRIS OS is building a graph-native, voice-first relationship intelligence system and autonomous fundraising agent spanning email, WhatsApp, phone, and web. The role strongly matches Paarth's production conversational-AI, agent orchestration, backend, cloud, evaluation, observability, workflow automation, and product-analytics experience. The primary blockers are CTO-level seniority and unresolved location terms: the canonical JOIN listing says London hybrid and €100,000, while Jack & Jill advertises remote and €70,000 plus equity.
strengths: Published hands-on Founding CTO / AI Engineer opening
Direct match for autonomous agents across WhatsApp, email, phone, and web
Strong overlap with production conversational AI, agent evaluation, tracing, feedback analysis, and large-scale interaction data
Renderperk demonstrates distributed backend ownership, queues, payments, storage, CI/CD, observability, and incident debugging
Role explicitly prioritizes AI governance, evaluation, safe deployment, privacy, transparency, and explainable matching
Product requires relationship graphs, structured data, workflow orchestration, contextual memory, and reliable tool execution
Compensation is materially above Paarth's target if eligibility and terms are genuine
Small founder-led team makes direct outreach and a proof-first proposal viable
gaps: No previous formal CTO or engineering-management title
No direct venture-capital relationship graph or fundraising-platform experience
Limited demonstrated bias-mitigation and privacy-preserving ML ownership
London hybrid and employee classification may exclude an India-based start
Role expects zero-to-one architecture plus future hiring and team leadership
Close European-hours requirement creates sustained timezone overlap
unknowns: Whether the role is London hybrid or genuinely remote
Whether remote work includes India and whether contracting is possible
Why JOIN lists €100,000 while Jack & Jill lists €70,000 plus equity
Equity percentage, vesting, cliff, and dilution terms
Current product maturity, active founders and investors, revenue, runway, and funding
Relationship-graph architecture, data sources, consent model, and data ownership
Current responsibilities and continued role of the existing Tech Lead
Bias evaluation methodology and legal basis for processing contact and relationship data
Whether a paid trial or internship-to-full-time structure is acceptable
evaluation.outreach_angle: Message founder Clarisse Beurrier with a technically specific proposal: position Paarth around production conversational agents, multi-channel integrations, tracing and evaluation, relationship/context systems, workflow reliability, and backend infrastructure. Acknowledge that the opening is CTO-level and ask whether she would consider a paid milestone-based trial leading into the founding role. Ask directly whether the role can begin remotely from India and which compensation listing is authoritative.
evaluation.proposed_artifact: Build a relationship-routing agent prototype using synthetic founder and investor profiles: graph-based thesis matching, explainable ranking, consent-aware contact paths, structured warm-introduction drafts, WhatsApp/email tool simulations, human approval before sending, idempotent outreach records, audit logs, evaluation for match quality and demographic bias, prompt-injection tests, and Langfuse-style traces with latency, cost, failure, and recovery metrics.

pipeline.next_action: Confirm remote-from-India eligibility and authoritative compensation with founder Clarisse Beurrier or COO Jacqueline Corsini; if viable, tailor the CV, outline the relationship-routing agent artifact, apply through JOIN, and send a differentiated founder message.
pipeline.notes: Do not apply blindly before resolving location. JOIN currently says London hybrid and €100,000/year; Jack & Jill says remote and €70,000 plus equity. No outreach or application has occurred.
